t:
(a) 
Exemption From Clearance Requirements.—Section 411 of the Unemployment Compensation Amendments of 1976 is amended by adding at the end thereof the following new subsection:

“(j) 
Exemption From Requirements for Office of Management and Budget Clearance.—

“(1) 
Federal reports act.—The requirements of chapter 35 of title 44, United States Code, shall not apply to the Commission.


“(2) 
Reports to congress.—Any reports submitted to the Congress by the Commission shall be submitted directly to the Congress and shall not be subject to any requirements for clearance of reports by the Office of Management and Budget.”.

 
    (b) 
Effective Date.—The amendment made by this section shall take effect on the date of the enactment of this Act.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that a reference to a "Commission" and its reports signals an advisory body with outside participation. But this section only exempts the Commission from Federal Reports Act requirements and OMB clearance when it reports to Congress. Both OMB and Congress are inside the federal government, and the section does not establish the Commission's membership or provide any comment period, hearing, consultation with outsiders, or right to sue.
fable.s: Any reports submitted to the Congress by the Commission shall be submitted directly to the Congress and shall not be subject to any requirements for clearance of reports by the Office of Management and Budget.

opus.w: The section only exempts the Commission from the chapter 35 clearance requirements and from OMB review of its reports to Congress. Reports to Congress and OMB clearance both stay inside the federal government. The section does not set up a comment period, a hearing, consultation with outsiders, or the Commission's membership. Mentioning a 'Commission' is not enough to count as outside participation.
opus.s: Any reports submitted to the Congress by the Commission shall be submitted directly to the Congress and shall not be subject to any requirements for clearance of reports by the Office of Management and Budget.
opus.b: The tempting reading is "Yes": the section mentions a "Commission" and its reports, which suggests an advisory body that might include outside members. That fails because this section doesn't create the Commission or say who sits on it. It only exempts the Commission from OMB paperwork clearance and lets it send reports straight to Congress, and Congress is inside the federal government.

qwen_chat.w: This section exempts a Commission from Office of Management and Budget (OMB) clearance requirements and allows it to submit reports directly to Congress. Both the OMB and Congress are part of the federal government. The definition explicitly states that reports to Congress or coordination between federal agencies are not participation. There is no mention of consulting with or coordinating with non-federal entities such as the public, states, or private organizations.
qwen_chat.s: Any reports submitted to the Congress by the Commission shall be submitted directly to the Congress and shall not be subject to any requirements for clearance of reports by the Office of Management and Budget.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the Commission submits reports to Congress, this involves interaction with an outside entity. However, the definition explicitly states that Congress is INSIDE the federal government, and reports to Congress are a common trap for "No". Furthermore, the section primarily exempts the Commission from OMB clearance, which is an internal executive branch process. There is no requirement for the Commission to consult with the public, states, or other non-federal entities before making decisions.
